item.title: Implement safe_extract.extract per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local chat): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Repository: quality-safe-extract (base main). Read SPEC.md at the repo root first; it is the authoritative contract. Current safe_extract.py is a stub and test_safe_extract.py has basic tests; keep the existing tests passing.

Summary of the contract (SPEC.md is the source of truth):
- Implement `extract(entries, root) -> list[str]`. entries: list of (name: str, data: bytes) tuples. Reject any non-list batch (tuples, iterators, generators, even empty) with ValueError, without consuming them or touching the filesystem.
- root: pathlib.Path or str naming an existing real directory (not a symlink).
- Validate the ENTIRE batch before creating any file or directory: malformed entries, non-string names, non-bytes data -> ValueError. Names: nonempty relative POSIX paths; reject leading '/', backslashes, colons, NUL, empty/'.'/'..' components. Do not sanitize, normalize or decode names; literal '%' is legal. Reject duplicate names and file/directory collisions within the batch in either order.
- Below root: no existing component may be a symlink (including dangling, and the target). Every existing ancestor must be a directory; each target must be absent. Never overwrite, never follow links, even to locations inside root. All conflicts and invalid roots -> ValueError.
- Validation failure must leave root and outside files unchanged. Empty batch returns [] after root validation. Valid batches create missing parent directories and write exact bytes (including empty files). Return names in input order.
- Unexpected filesystem I/O errors must propagate visibly (no swallowing). Use only the Python standard library.

Required work:
- Implement safe_extract.py with the documented API. Keep functions under 60 lines, validate at the boundary, and avoid hidden failure (no bare except/pass).
- Add focused tests in test_safe_extract.py (unittest or pytest-compatible, standard library) covering every rejection rule above, the boundary cases (empty batch, non-list containers left unconsumed, empty file, '%' names, str vs Path root, root symlink, symlink ancestor, dangling symlink target, pre-existing file/target conflict, collisions in both orders, validation failure leaving the filesystem unchanged, nested parent creation) and the happy path.
- Run the tests and confirm they pass before committing.

Git: commit the work on the item's branch with a clear message. Use the repository's configured git identity; do not override it. Do NOT add any Claude, Claude Code, or generated-by attribution lines to commits or PR text (the operator's CLAUDE.md forbids it). Do not push.
